result.title: Speaking-Clock Mamba: Phoneme-Conditioned State-Space Modeling for Visual Forced Alignment
result.summary: Visual forced alignment (VFA) locates phoneme and word boundaries in a silent talking-face video given its transcript. Existing methods mainly enforce transcript order at the decoding stage, leaving the encoder without an explicit mechanism to anchor its temporally evolving representation to transcript progress. As a result, phoneme-specific evidence is blurred and alignment drift accumulates over long sequences. In this paper, we propose Speaking-Clock Mamba, which makes transcript progress part of the temporal recurrence. A selective state-space (Mamba) backbone is inserted between the visual frontend and the Conformer cross-attention encoder, and a Phoneme-Conditioned Selective Scan (PCSS) conditions its input-dependent step size on a supervised, structurally monotone speaking clock that estimates progress through the transcript. Since causal and bidirectional variants of this backbone make complementary errors, a training-free selector picks the more confident alignment per utterance. Experiments on LRS2 and LRS3 show consistent gains over protocol-matched baselines, and the supervised clock provides an explicit estimate of alignment progress.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Speaking-Clock Mamba，在视觉前端与 Conformer 之间插入选择性状态空间主干，用受监督的单调「说话时钟」条件化其输入相关扫描步长，定位静音说话视频中的音素与词边界，并以免训练方式在因果/双向变体间按置信度择一。
AI.relevance_reason: 将单调进度信号注入循环状态更新，可能与 LVR 中依赖长度的进度表示、状态演化与停止决策相关；因果与双向变体的互补误差及置信选择也可供核查多种 latent 假设的聚合与筛选。
